level1.text: A kettle transforms $1.80 \cdot 10^{5}\,\text{J}$ of electrical energy in $90.0\,\text{s}$. Calculate the power of the kettle.
The power of an LED lamp is $8.0\,\text{W}$. How much energy does the lamp transform in $5.0\,\text{s}$?
The power of a microwave oven is $1200\,\text{W}$. How long does it take for the oven to transform $72\,000\,\text{J}$ of energy?

The graph shows the electrical energy transformed by two devices, A and B, as a function of time, and each device transforms energy steadily. Read two points from the line that rises more steeply. What is the power of this device? Give the answer in watts.
The power of a heater is $1.5\,\text{kW}$, and it is on for $2.0\,\text{h}$. How much energy does it consume in kilowatt-hours?

level2.text: The power of an electric sauna heater is $6.0\,\text{kW}$, and it is on for $150\,\text{min}$. The price of electricity is $20\,\text{c/kWh}$, that is $0.20\,\text{€/kWh}$. How much does heating the sauna cost? Give the answer in euros.
A phone battery can hold $15\,\text{Wh}$ of energy. Give the energy in joules.
A device consumes $0.40\,\text{kWh}$ of energy in $20\,\text{min}$. Calculate the average power of the device in watts.

In a shop six emergency exit lights are on, each at a power of $1.5\,\text{W}$, for the whole year. A year has $8760\,\text{h}$. How much energy do the lights consume in a year in total? Give the answer in kilowatt-hours.

level3.text: A light is on for $4.0\,\text{h}$ a day for the whole year, $365\,\text{days}$. An old incandescent bulb ($60\,\text{W}$) is replaced with an LED lamp ($8.0\,\text{W}$). The price of electricity is $20\,\text{c/kWh}$, that is $0.20\,\text{€/kWh}$. How many euros are saved in a year?

A household consumes $3.0 \cdot 10^{3}\,\text{kWh}$ of electrical energy in a year. A year has $8760\,\text{h}$. Calculate the average power of the household in watts. Is it greater or smaller than the sum of the rated powers of the household's appliances, and why?

An electric car consumes $18\,\text{kWh}$ per hundred kilometres when driving. The car is charged from a wall socket at a power of $2.3\,\text{kW}$ for $8.0\,\text{h}$. How far can the car drive on the charging energy when charging losses are ignored?
